clinician.trajectory_summary: A 63-year-old Hispanic male with no significant past medical history presented to the ED with one week of left lower extremity swelling and pain. He had already been prescribed rivaroxaban by his PCP prior to ED arrival. On admission, lower extremity Doppler ultrasound revealed occlusive DVT in the left calf extending to the left femoral vein, with involvement of the saphenous veins, and chronic occlusive DVT in the right popliteal veins. A venogram was performed during admission, which confirmed the diagnosis of May-Thurner Syndrome with patent distal IVC and catheter tip positioned in the IVC. Tissue plasminogen activator (tPA) infusion at 1 mg per hour was initiated via the infusion catheter on admission. By hospital day 3, the patient reported symptomatic improvement and was discharged home on chronic anticoagulation with rivaroxaban.
